title: Understanding Expository Dialogue
use_cases: Use when conveying essential backstory through natural character interaction
Use when clarifying complex plot points without using external narration
Use when establishing the rules or history of a fictional world
Implement when bridging gaps in the audience's knowledge of past events
content:
Expository dialogue is a crucial element in screenwriting, serving as a tool to convey essential information to the audience. However, it can be a double-edged sword: when done well, it seamlessly integrates into the narrative, but when mishandled, it can disrupt the story's flow and feel forced or artificial.

Expository dialogue refers to conversations between characters that provide background information, clarify plot points, or establish context. Its primary purpose is to inform the audience about the story's world, characters, and events without relying on narration or other non-diegetic elements.
